en: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths among which was that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "While a man was strutting in two garments..." then he mentioned the like of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Mughirah—meaning al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "While a man was strutting, walking in his two cloaks (burdayh), admiring himself, Allah caused the earth to swallow him up, so he sinks tumbling down into it until the Day of Resurrection."

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us; all of them said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with something similar to this.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sallam al-Jumahi narrated to us, al-Rabi'—meaning Ibn Muslim—narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "While a man was walking, admiring his hair that reached his shoulders (jummah) and his two cloaks, suddenly the earth was made to swallow him up, so he sinks tumbling into the earth until the Hour is established."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us, Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, both from Shu'bah, with this chain of narration; and in the hadith of Ibn Ja'far: "Marwan used to appoint Abu Hurayrah as deputy," and in the hadith of Ibn al-Muthanna: "Abu Hurayrah used to be appointed deputy over Medina."

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad—who is Ibn Ziyad—who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah, having seen a man dragging his waist-wrapper and stamping the ground with his foot, while he was governor over Bahrain, saying: "The governor has come! The governor has come!" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Allah will not look at one who drags his waist-wrapper out of arrogance."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Muhammad informed me, from 'Abdullah ibn Waqid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I passed by the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while my waist-wrapper was hanging down, so he said: "O 'Abdullah, pull up your waist-wrapper." So I pulled it up. Then he said: "Pull it up further." So I pulled it up further, and I continued to observe that ever since. Some of the people asked: "To where?" He replied: "To the middle of the shins."

Muhammad ibn Hatim, Harun ibn 'Abdullah, and Ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to me—and their wordings are close—they said: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far saying: I instructed Muslim ibn Yasar, the freed slave of Nafi' ibn 'Abd al-Harith, to ask Ibn 'Umar—he said: while I was sitting between them: "Did you hear anything from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) concerning the one who drags his waist-wrapper out of pride?" He said: I heard him saying: "Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik—meaning Ibn Abi Sulayman—narrated to us; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abu Yunus narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, Ibrahim—meaning Ibn Nafi'—narrated to me; all of them from Muslim ibn Yannaq, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it, except that in the hadith of Abu Yunus it is "from Muslim Abu al-Hasan," and in all their narrations: "Whoever drags his waist-wrapper (izarahu)," and they did not say "his garment (thawbahu)."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, he said: I heard Muslim ibn Yannaq narrating from Ibn 'Umar, that he saw a man dragging his waist-wrapper, so he asked: "Who are you from?" He traced his lineage for him, and behold, he was a man from Banu Layth, and Ibn 'Umar recognized him. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with these two ears of mine saying: "Whoever drags his waist-wrapper intending nothing thereby except vanity, indeed Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan narrated to us, he said: I heard Salim say: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying... the like of it, except that he said: "his clothes (thiyabahu)."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Hanzalah narrated to us, he said: I heard Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever drags his garment out of pride, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from al-Shaybani; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, both from Muharib ibn Dithar and Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with the like of their hadith.

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us, 'Umar ibn Muhammad informed me, from his father, Salim ibn 'Abdullah, and Nafi', from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, the one who drags his garments out of pride, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Usamah narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, they said: Yahya—who is al-Qattan—narrated to us; all of them from 'Ubaydullah; (H) and Abu al-Rabi' and Abu Kamil narrated to us, they said: Hammad narrated to us; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Isma'il narrated to us, both from Ayyub; (H) and Qutaybah and Ibn Rumh narrated to us, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd; (H) and Harun al-Ayli narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Usamah narrated to me; all of these from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with the like of the hadith of Malik, and they added therein: "on the Day of Resurrection."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Nafi', 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, and Zayd ibn Aslam, all informing him from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah will not look at one who drags his garment out of pride."

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Hani' narrated to me that he heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman saying from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "There should be a bed for a man, a bed for his wife, a third for a guest, and a fourth is for Satan."
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to me, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, with this chain of narration, and he added: "so I let her be."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: When I got married, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me: "Have you acquired patterned carpets (anmat)?" I said: "Where would we get patterned carpets from?" He said: "Behold, they will soon be." Jabir said: "Now my wife has a patterned carpet, and I say to her: 'Remove it from me,' and she says: 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: They will soon be.'"

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, 'Amr al-Naqid, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is that of 'Amr—'Amr and Qutaybah said: "narrated to us," and Ishaq said: "Sufyan informed us," from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me when I got married: "Have you acquired patterned carpets (anmat)?" I said: "Where would we get patterned carpets from?" He said: "Behold, they will soon be."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us, Ibn Numayr narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, both from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, with this chain of narration, and they both said: "the bedding (dija') of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)"; and in the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah: "upon which he slept."

'Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di narrated to me, 'Ali ibn Mushir informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The bedding of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) upon which he slept was merely tanned leather stuffed with palm fibers.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The pillow of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) upon which he reclined was made of tanned leather stuffed with palm fibers.

Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to me, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from his father; (H) and Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to me, Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us; (H) and Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, my father informed me, from Mus'ab ibn Shaybah, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) went out one morning wearing a patterned woolen cloak (mirt murajjal) of black hair.
Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, with this chain of narration, the like of it, and he said: "a coarse waist-wrapper."

'Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di, Muhammad ibn Hatim, and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, all from Ibn 'Ulayyah—Ibn Hujr said: Isma'il narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Burdah, who said: 'A'ishah brought out to us a waist-wrapper and a patched cloak (kisa' mulabbad) and said: "In this the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed away." Ibn Hatim said in his hadith: "a coarse waist-wrapper."

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Abu Burdah, who said: I entered upon 'A'ishah, and she brought out to us a coarse waist-wrapper of the kind made in Yemen and a cloak of the kind they call patched (mulabbadah)—he said: and she swore by Allah that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed away in these two garments.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The most beloved of garments to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was the Hibarah (a striped Yemeni cloth).

Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, he said: We said to Anas ibn Malik: "Which clothing was most beloved to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—or most pleasing to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" He said: "The Hibarah (a striped Yemeni cloth)."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu al-Ahwas informed us, from 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from Abu Burdah, who said: 'Ali said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade me from wearing a ring on this finger of mine or this one—he said: and he pointed to the middle finger and the one next to it.
